{{Use mdy dates|cs1-dates=ly|date=October 2020}}{{Use list-defined references|date=October 2020}}'''Maggie Xiaoyan Cheng''' is an [[applied mathematics|applied mathematician]] and [[computer scientist]] who works as a professor of applied mathematics at the [[Illinois Institute of Technology]], where she directs the Center for Interdisciplinary Scientific Computation. Her research interests include [[cyber security]] and [[Machine Learning]].<ref name=iit>{{citation|url=https://www.iit.edu/directory/people/maggie-cheng|title=Maggie Cheng|work=Directory|publisher=Illinois Institute of Technology|accessdate=2020-11-04}}</ref>

==Education and career==
Cheng has a bachelor's and master's degree from the [[Beihang University|Beijing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics]].<ref name=cv>{{citation|url=http://math.iit.edu/~mcheng8/ChengCV.pdf|title=Curriculum vitae|accessdate=2020-11-04}}</ref> She completed a Ph.D. in computer science in 2003 from the [[University of Minnesota]].<ref name=ieee>{{citation|url=https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/author/37086261748|title=Maggie X. Cheng|work=IEEE Xplore|publisher=IEEE|accessdate=2020-11-04}}</ref>

After completing her doctorate, she became an assistant professor of computer science at the [[Missouri University of Science and Technology]]. She moved to the Martin Tuchman School of Management of the [[New Jersey Institute of Technology]] in 2016,{{r|cv}} and moved to the Illinois Institute of Technology in 2018,<ref name=welcome>{{citation|url=https://today.iit.edu/the-department-of-applied-mathematics-welcomes-two-new-faculty-members/|title=Department of Applied Mathematics Welcomes Two New Faculty Members|date=November 1, 2018|work=Illinois Tech Today|accessdate=2020-11-04}}</ref> and she was promoted to full professor in 2020.{{r|cv}}
